title: California state workers announce statewide one-day walkout

tea.why: Protesting alleged bad-faith bargaining practices by Governor Gavin Newsom's administration during labor negotiations.
tea.want: Demanding a 20% wage increase over three years, flexible telework options, in-office stipends, and higher healthcare contributions.
tea.changed: Oct 7: SEIU Local 1000 officially called for a one-day statewide strike for the upcoming Wednesday.

summary: Tens of thousands of California state government workers represented by SEIU Local 1000 are scheduled to participate in a statewide one-day walkout. The job action comes after the union's previous three-year contract expired on June 30 and negotiations with Governor Gavin Newsom's administration stalled. The union accuses the state of bargaining in bad faith through mass rejections of proposals and has filed charges with the Public Employment Relations Board. The planned strike is expected to affect public-facing services such as the DMV, unemployment offices, food assistance, and state parks across multiple cities, including Sacramento and Eureka. The state previously asked PERB for a temporary restraining order to block the strike, but the request was rejected.
demands: Wage increases of about 20% across three years
Stipends for workers required to work in-office
Increased state contributions toward healthcare costs
response: The state asked the Public Employment Relations Board to issue a temporary restraining order to halt the walkout, arguing impasse mediations should finish first, but PERB rejected the request.

updates.text: SEIU Local 1000 announced a one-day statewide strike following a 96.2% approval vote by members.
